sentences.text: Somebody said the pacing sagged; somebody else defended the sag as the whole point. Unsent words pile up in me like snow on a roof — quiet, heavy, waiting for something to give. There's an etiquette question here: do we critique the darkness itself, or only how convincingly it's rendered? Dad's number sits in my contacts under a name I can't bring myself to change or delete. Professor Okafor timed our praise: two minutes each, then straight into what the middle chapters refuse to do. Our falling-out had witnesses; the estrangement has none — it just happens to me quietly, on repeat, in kitchens. Whose despair is on the page, Priya kept asking — the character's, or merely the syntax's? Every December I buy her favorite marzipan, then eat it alone in January. Is it cruelty or craft when the narrator describes his own unraveling in such flat, clinical declaratives? Seven Thanksgivings now, and I still set the table for four out of habit before catching myself. "Please stop saying relatable," Okafor sighed, "and tell me what the third chapter actually does." Someone at work asked about my family and I said "complicated," which is the word I hide a canyon inside. Reading it aloud, you hear the paragraph rhythms shorten as Ada's world narrows — that's the manuscript's best trick. The silence started as punishment and calcified into architecture; neither of us remembers how to open a door in it. Marisol flipped to page twelve and asked why the mirror scene arrives before we ever learn what Ada has lost. Some nights I read our last texts from 2019 like an accident report, looking for the exact moment of impact. After the break the discussion turned technical — free indirect discourse, and whether Ada's thoughts bleed too easily into the narrator's. Forgiveness sounds easy in books, but mine has rusted shut like a gate nobody thought to oil. By workshop rules the author sat silent, underlining furiously while we argued about her ending. Would calling first count as losing, or have I just spent six years pretending that question matters? I want to write a suicide letter.
